title: 村居（草长莺飞二月天）
author: 高鼎
intro: Grass growing, birds flying, willows swaying — and children racing home from school to fly kites in the spring wind. A bright, simple poem that every Chinese primary-school pupil learns.
analysis: 这首诗写早春二月乡村的景色和孩子们放风筝的快乐。前两句写景：小草长出来了，黄莺在天上飞，杨柳的长枝轻轻拂过河堤，在春天淡淡的雾气里好像喝醉了一样。“醉”字用得很妙，这是拟人（把东西当作人来写），让杨柳有了人的样子，也写出春天让人陶醉的感觉。后两句写人：孩子们放学回来得早，赶紧趁着东风把风筝放上天。“忙趁”两个字写出孩子们急急忙忙、兴高采烈的样子。全诗前半写景、后半写人，景美人乐，充满生机，语言浅显，是小学生最早学的古诗之一。
analysisEn: This poem shows a village in early spring, the second month of the lunar calendar, and the fun children have flying kites. The first two lines are the scenery: new grass is growing, orioles are flying, and the long branches of the willows brush along the riverbank, swaying as if drunk in the soft spring haze. The word 醉 (“drunk”) is a lovely touch — it is personification, describing a thing as if it were a person, and it suggests how intoxicating spring feels. The last two lines are about people: the children have come home from school early and hurry to catch the east wind and send their paper kites up into the sky. The words 忙趁 (“rush to take advantage of”) capture their excitement perfectly. The first half paints the scene, the second half fills it with people; the landscape is beautiful and the people are happy, and the whole poem is full of life. Because the language is so plain, it is one of the first classical poems Chinese children learn at primary school.
background: Gao Ding (1828–1880) was a late-Qing poet from Zhejiang about whom little is known. He is said to have written this poem while living in the countryside; today it is his only widely known work.
pronunciation: 草长莺飞：统编教材注 zhǎng（生长），也有人读 cháng。拂堤 fú dī；散学 sàn；纸鸢 yuān。

lines.py: cǎo zhǎng yīng fēi èr yuè tiān
lines.lit: Grass grows, orioles fly — the days of the second month;
lines.en: Grass springing up and orioles in flight — the second month is here;

lines.py: fú dī yáng liǔ zuì chūn yān
lines.lit: Brushing the bank, the willows are drunk in spring mist.
lines.en: willows brush the riverbank, swaying drunk in the spring haze.

lines.py: ér tóng sàn xué guī lái zǎo
lines.lit: The children, school dismissed, come home early;
lines.en: The children are home from school early today,

lines.py: máng chèn dōng fēng fàng zhǐ yuān
lines.lit: busily taking advantage of the east wind to fly paper kites.
lines.en: racing to catch the east wind and fly their paper kites.

words.note: 黄莺，叫声好听，是春天的鸟。
农历二月，大约是公历三月。
不是烟，是春天水边的雾气。

words.en: to finish school for the day

words.note: 现代汉语仍用，如“趁热吃”。
现代汉语说“风筝”。鸢是一种鹰。

imagery.name: 草
imagery.zh: 小草长出来，是早春最先出现的生机。
imagery.en: New grass is the first sign of life returning in early spring.

imagery.name: 柳
imagery.zh: 杨柳轻拂河堤，像醉了一样摇摆，写出春天的柔美和陶醉。
imagery.en: Willows brushing the bank and swaying as if drunk — the softness and intoxication of spring.

imagery.name: 春风
imagery.zh: 东风是春风，孩子们趁着它放风筝，带来欢乐。
imagery.en: The east wind is the spring wind — the children ride it to send their kites up.
